again.accept: A report came. If you are happy with it, finish the task with “{{finish}}”.
again.answer: The AI carried on and has a question for you. Answer it as before.
again.question: The AI on the task has a question for you. Press this row to open it.
again.received: The front-desk AI has it, and is passing it to the AI on the task.
again.result: The AI on the task sent a report. Press this row to open it.
again.working: The AI has your instructions and is carrying on. A question or report for you moves the task back to “{{section}}”.

guide.closed: The guide has ended. You can show it again from {{settings}} → {{tab}}, under “{{guide}}”.
guide.example:
This is a demo to try the alpacawork flow.
Create an HTML page that shows "Hello" in two fonts, then ask me which one is better.
guide.moreExample: Make one more version so I can compare them.
guide.over: That's the end of the getting-started guide. You can show it again from {{settings}} → {{tab}}, under “{{guide}}”.

say.accept: If you are happy with it, finish the task with this button ({{finish}}). To ask for more, send another instruction instead of finishing.
say.anotherRepository: To use another repository, open this, choose “{{create}}”, and pick that repository as its working folder.
say.answer: A question from the AI on the task (the owner). Press an option and the answer goes into the input box below. Send it as is to answer. You can also write your own reply instead.
say.conversation: Chats with the front-desk AI are disposable. Once they pile up, open the conversation and clear it with “{{clear}}”. Before clearing, ask for anything worth keeping to be made a task.
say.direct: The front-desk AI answers short questions right here. Ask for a job, like “make …”, and it becomes a task in the list. The front-desk AI decides which it is.
say.label: This label tells the AI which task or project you mean. Without it, the AI works it out from the conversation. Try removing it and sending your request.
say.more: Once you have looked over the report, you can keep asking. Try having it make one more version to compare.
say.phone: Using it from your phone is what we recommend most. You can send instructions from anywhere, and answer a question by picking a choice and swiping. The steps are in {{settings}} under “{{apps}}”.
say.phoneGrip: Drag the handle up or down to change the height.
say.phoneNotify: Notifications are off on this phone. Turn them on to be notified when a question or a report arrives.
say.phoneQuestion: Choose an answer, then swipe right to send it, or left for “{{hold}}”. Bring your finger back partway and nothing happens.
say.phoneResult: Swipe right for “{{finish}}”, left for “{{hold}}”. Bring your finger back partway and nothing happens.
say.question: Your turn. The AI on the task has a question. Press this row to open it.
say.received: The front-desk AI (the coordinator) has it: it is the one you talk to here. When it is a job, it turns it into a task and passes it to an AI to own it (the owner).
say.result: A report came. It means the AI on the task has finished its work. Press this row to open it.
say.send: This is the only input box. Every request and instruction goes here. The front-desk AI (the coordinator) receives it.
say.sendAgain: Write what you want done here and send it.
say.stop: To stop the AI, choose “{{stop}}” here, or ask in the input box. You can ask there to change settings, too.
say.unassigned: No AI is on this task yet. Open the row and ask in the input box to start it, and an AI takes it on.
say.working: This is a task. Each task has its own AI (the owner), which calls in helper AIs (members) when it needs them. When a question or report makes it your turn, the task moves to “{{section}}”.

speed.help: How to read the output speed
speed.helpBars: The bars show the last minute in 5-second steps.
speed.helpSpeed: How fast the working agents output tokens (last 5 seconds' average).
speed.helpZero: A 0 that stays may mean the agent is waiting for a command or the like to finish (a screen recording, a GitHub run). Open the task to see what it waits on.

Output speed {{rate}} tok/s (last 5 seconds' average)
Last minute: average {{mean}}, peak {{peak}}

speed.totalTip_other: Total output speed of {{count}} tasks in progress (last 5 seconds' average)

pending.long: A new instruction arrived. Waiting for the owner to give a new report estimate.

timeView.axisAbsent: The time view is not saved on this device. It loads when the connection is back.
timeView.help: Scroll sideways to move through time. Zoom with ctrl (⌘) + wheel, a pinch, or two fingers. Double-click the time scale to see everything. Point at a line (tap on a phone) for details. Keys: + − 0 N; press → on a title to read its lines in turn.

welcome.lead: A place to hand work to a team of AIs.
